subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's guarded promotion of standalone `antml:`/`mm:` attribute-dialect XML text into executable tool calls, plus the additive `preserveCodeRegions` Plugin SDK option?
rationale: Automation can verify parser shape and tests, but only maintainers can decide whether the execution-boundary repair and public SDK option are the intended product/API contract.

options.title: Accept Guarded Promotion
options.body: Land this approach after a fresh rebase/check cycle, using the closed namespace allow-list, allowed-tool-name gating, strict SDK default, and current tests as the contract.

options.title: Narrow To Sanitization
options.body: Remove or defer automatic promotion and only strip leaked XML, reducing execution-boundary risk while leaving some degraded turns unrecovered.

options.title: Keep Code-Aware Mode Internal
options.body: Retain internal code-region preservation but drop the public SDK option if maintainers do not want to expand the plugin-facing API now.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Promotion
recommendation.body: Land this approach after a fresh rebase/check cycle, using the closed namespace allow-list, allowed-tool-name gating, strict SDK default, and current tests as the contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice crosses shared sanitizer behavior and Plugin SDK/provider-stream seams where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
